1941-06-22.headline: Barbarossa
1941-06-22.summary: Three million men, 3,500 tanks and 2,700 aircraft attack along a front of 1,600 km — the largest invasion in history. The Soviet air force loses around 1,200 aircraft on the first day, most of them on the ground.

events.name: Brest
events.text: The fortress garrison fights on for a week behind the front.

events.name: Minsk
events.text: Two Panzer groups drive for Minsk on the first morning.

1941-06-28.headline: Minsk
1941-06-28.summary: The first great encirclement closes: around 300,000 men taken. The pattern of the summer is set — armour closes the pockets, infantry marches to catch up, and the Red Army loses armies faster than it can count them.

events.name: Minsk
events.text: Taken on the sixth day, 350 km from the frontier.

1941-07-03.headline: Stalin speaks
1941-07-03.summary: After eleven days of silence Stalin broadcasts, addressing the country as brothers and sisters, and orders a scorched earth. It is the first time the war is called patriotic rather than ideological.

events.name: Moscow
events.text: Everything of use is to be destroyed or moved east. 1,500 factories are moved beyond the Urals.

1941-08-08.headline: Smolensk
1941-08-08.summary: The pocket at Smolensk yields another 300,000 prisoners, but takes two months instead of two weeks. It is the first sign the timetable is slipping.

events.name: Smolensk
events.text: The road to Moscow is open. Hitler turns south instead.

1941-09-08.headline: Leningrad is cut off
1941-09-08.summary: The last land route closes. The siege lasts 872 days and kills something like a million civilians, most of them in the first winter, most of them of starvation.

events.name: Leningrad
events.text: No assault: the city is to be starved out. Rations fall to 125 grams of bread a day.

1941-09-26.headline: Kiev
1941-09-26.summary: The largest encirclement ever achieved by any army: around 600,000 prisoners. It is a total victory that costs the Germans the campaigning weather they needed for Moscow.

events.name: Kiev
events.text: Four Soviet armies destroyed. Ten days later the rains begin.

1941-10-08.headline: The mud
1941-10-08.summary: The autumn rasputitsa turns every unpaved road in western Russia to liquid mud. Wheeled transport stops entirely. The advance on Moscow waits for the ground to freeze — and then finds out what a Russian winter is.

events.name: Vyazma
events.text: Another 600,000 taken at Vyazma and Bryansk, into ground no lorry can cross.

1941-10-20.headline: Moscow under siege
1941-10-20.summary: A state of siege is declared. The government, the diplomatic corps and Lenin's body leave for Kuibyshev. Stalin stays, and the fact that he stays is worth divisions.

events.name: Moscow
events.text: Panic and looting for two days, then curfew and summary justice.

1941-11-07.headline: The parade
1941-11-07.summary: Troops parade through Red Square on the anniversary of the revolution and march directly from it to the front, thirty kilometres away.

events.name: Moscow
events.text: Held under falling snow that grounded the Luftwaffe.

1941-11-20.headline: Rostov
1941-11-20.summary: Rostov-on-Don is taken. Nine days later the Soviets take it back — the first German retreat of the war, and the first order Hitler gives to hold ground at any cost.

events.name: Rostov
events.text: Taken on 21 November, lost again on 29 November.

1941-12-05.headline: The high-water mark
1941-12-05.summary: Reconnaissance troops see the spires of Moscow through field glasses at thirty degrees below zero, in summer uniforms. That night the temperature drops further, and the next morning a hundred fresh Siberian divisions attack.

events.name: Moscow
events.text: The closest German troops get. The counteroffensive opens on 6 December.
